handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For pax8 the manifest gained: PAX8_AUDIENCE, PAX8_BASE_URL, PAX8_TOKEN_URL. server.json gained: PAX8_AUDIENCE, PAX8_BASE_URL, PAX8_TOKEN_URL. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: PAX8_AUDIENCE, PAX8_BASE_URL, PAX8_TOKEN_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: PAX8_NO_CONFIG_WRITE makes every credential write a no-op (token cache included) while leaving the `auth logout` erase working, and the MCP server honours it too (issue #270)
handfixes.why: Issue #270, raised by @Xenith-B off the back of #266. #266 stopped env-supplied client credentials reaching disk; the MINTED access token still landed in ~/.config/<tool>-cli/config.toml in cleartext and there was no supported way to turn that off. Their workaround was `--config NUL`, which is OS-specific, undocumented, makes doctor report a false 'not configured', and - the part that matters most - does not cover the MCP servers at all, because internal/mcp resolved its own hardcoded config path and ignored --config. Three deliberate boundaries make this switch honest rather than merely quiet. (1) ClearTokens keeps calling save() directly: it is the ERASE path, and routing it through the guard would make `auth logout` silently inert, which is a worse defect than the one being fixed. (2) `auth login` and `auth set-token` REFUSE and name the variable rather than reporting a save that did not happen - a false success is the same defect class as a doctor that says credentials are fine without checking. (3) newMCPClient now resolves through config.Load(""), the resolver the CLI uses, so the MCP server honours both PAX8_CONFIG and this switch; that is the half the issue says is uncovered today. The variable is declared on all three install channels because for a Claude Desktop install the manifest prompt is the ONLY channel that can set an environment variable. Class C, new documented surface. GENERATOR-class: a reprint drops the switch entirely and silently restores the plaintext token cache.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit <PREFIX>_NO_CONFIG_WRITE (or an equivalent) as part of the standard config surface, with the same three boundaries: the erase path exempt, explicit save commands failing loudly rather than no-oping, and the MCP server resolving its config through config.Load("") instead of a hardcoded home-relative path. The hardcoded path in internal/mcp/tools.go is a generator defect in its own right - it makes --config and <PREFIX>_CONFIG inert for every MCP install on every connector.

asserts.contains: | `auth login` / `auth set-token` | Refuse, naming the variable, instead of reporting a save that did not happen. |

handfixes.summary: Every token request (auth login, the automatic client-credentials mint and the refresh grant) goes through cliutil.OAuthTokenHTTPClient, which follows same-origin redirects only, so the client secret never reaches a host a redirect from the token URL names
handfixes.why: Owner decision on PR #441 (finish the auth-wire class). `auth login` (through http.DefaultClient) and the automatic client-credentials mint and refresh grant (through c.HTTPClient, whose CheckRedirect follows a 307 to another host) replayed the token request body, the client secret included, to whatever host a redirect from the token URL named. Printed before press 4.33.5, which routes every token request through cliutil.OAuthTokenHTTPClient (a token client that follows same-origin hops only); this back-ports that file verbatim and uses it at the same call sites. TestAuthLoginRefusesATokenRedirectToAnotherOrigin and TestTokenMintRefusesARedirectToAnotherOrigin failed on the previous commit (the second host received the token request) and pass now. The host compare is also hardened (see the newer-print entries): an IP literal compares exactly, IPv6 zone included; a DNS name folds ASCII case only.

handfixes.summary: Both client_credentials token requests (the automatic mint and `auth login`) send audience=api://p8p.client (overridable with PAX8_AUDIENCE) from one form builder; press 4.34.2 does not emit it
handfixes.why: Pax8's token manager (https://token-manager.pax8.com/oauth/token) requires an audience on the client_credentials request (the hand edit's own comment: without it the mint is rejected or yields an unusable token, so every command fails auth). client.go carries a hand-added resolveClientCredentialsAudience() (PAX8_AUDIENCE, default api://p8p.client) and mintClientCredentials sets it on the form. Press 4.34.0's client.go.tmpl has no audience support and no spec extension expresses one (first noted on the 4.22 reprint as not absorbed upstream), so a reprint regenerates client.go without it. The install-credentials-declared-on-every-channel entry pins only the PAX8_AUDIENCE declarations in manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md: a reprint that dropped the code would leave PAX8_AUDIENCE declared but unread. check_env_schema.py then fails, but its fix hint ('Drop it everywhere if the binary no longer reads it') steers toward deleting the declarations, which would remove the override for good; this entry instead fails check_handfixes.py at the dropped lines and names the hand edit to restore. These asserts are code_only so a doc comment naming the function cannot satisfy them. pax8 4.34.2 reprint: the shipped `auth login` minted without the audience, so the token it saved was unusable; both mint paths now build their body with client.ClientCredentialsTokenForm (token-request-body-credentials).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press fix: an OAuth audience on the client-credentials security scheme (an x-auth-audience style extension with an env override) rendered into the token form by client.go.tmpl.

handfixes.summary: Each credential goes only to the host it is bound to: the bearer token and every API request to the origin of PAX8_BASE_URL; the client ID and secret only to the API base URL's origin or Pax8's token manager (https://token-manager.pax8.com, the kit's Origins, so a PAX8_TOKEN_URL on any other host is refused before anything is sent), whose origin receives nothing but a POST to that exact path with no Authorization header; every redirect hop stays on the origin of the request it follows. handfixes.summary: The novels share one reading of each documented Pax8 shape (internal/cli/pax8_novel_rules.go): Subscription.status classified over the whole enum (Active, Activated, Trial bill; unknown statuses never count and are reported); Subscription.billingTerm (MRR is Monthly only; Annual, 2-Year, 3-Year reported beside it per term; One-Time, Activation, Trial excluded); one timestamp parser (numeric offsets with or without a colon; an unreadable date is never in a window); every collection read under the names sync and live reads store it as (usage summaries are the subscriptions_usage_summaries dependent); reconcile joins invoice lines to subscriptions by subscriptionId (a line for a period before a non-billing subscription ended is history; free trials, and in --draft mode non-monthly terms, are not expected on an invoice). After the Codex stop rule (unreviewed): a record stored under two names is read once, newest row first; a trial priced above zero bills; credit lines (InvoiceItem.type rebate, payment-credit, service-credit, invoice-credit, or a negative total) neither bill nor count as billed.

handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand and replaces this connector's own credential layer. internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one Declarations literal (SecretEnv PAX8_CLIENT_ID, PAX8_CLIENT_SECRET, PAX8_COOKIE and PAX8_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN; URLEnv PAX8_TOKEN_URL and PAX8_FEEDBACK_ENDPOINT; Files = the config the run really uses first, then the 0600 credential store and the legacy config, with every other config, store and profiles.json any --config or --home could mean held through cliutil.HoldFile (a profile store through cliutil.HoldProfileFile); CredentialFlags --client-id and --client-secret; StdinFlags --stdin; ResponseFields access_token, refresh_token and id_token; BaseURL PAX8_BASE_URL, default https://api.pax8.com/v1; Origins the base URL for everything, the base URL and Pax8's token manager for the client pair, nowhere for the cookie and the MCP HTTP token). credkit.Start is the first statement of both mains and credkit.Exit ends them. Every sink is routed: stdout and stderr at the descriptor; the API client (client.OutboundGuard, under the origin pin in pax8_guard.go), feedback, deliver and the probe through credkit.Transport; cache, journal, teach log, learnings audit, profile, platform profile, rate-limit lock, download and export files through credkit.WriteFile, AppendFile, OpenFile and NewWriter; SQLite through internal/credsql (credkit.SQLDriver, the MCP sql value cap set as each connection opens); the MCP server through MCPTools, MCPIn, MCPOut and MCPHTTP; the MCP server's CLI child through RunCommand; terminal checks through credkit.Terminal; auth set-token holds the token it reads from stdin, and a minted token is held where it is minted. The 0600 credential store and config.toml are credential sources: their writes are a declared exemption, outside the kit in cliutil.AtomicWriteCredentialFile, and both are in Files.
handfixes.why: Retires secret-echo-decoded-funnel, output-chokepoint, file-sinks-withheld, store-never-keeps-secrets, mcp-protocol-messages-withheld, network-sinks-withheld, startup-output-held-first, mcp-held-arguments-refused, undecoded-encodings-every-alignment, held-forms-in-every-encoding, response-credentials-held, every-text-encoding-withheld, outbound-split-parts-refused, auth-carrier-names-and-shapes-held, replaced by the shared credential kit (entries removed: the ledger's retired list only takes retirements tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json backs). The connector's own holder, output chokepoint, secret funnel, encodings table and outbound checks kept growing per review round because each sink and encoding was closed one at a time; the kit is one shared implementation of the leak contract, checked byte for byte against tools/maintainer/credkit (vendor_credkit.py --check). It closes the classes Codex r2 left open, each kept with its failing input in internal/pax8blackbox/kit_r2_test.go against the built binary: a partly escaped secret mixed with plain text in output, hex of each half of the secret in two query values of feedback --send (reaches the server 0 times), and one value of PAX8_COOKIE printed on its own. handfixes.summary: The learn journal keeps no text the operator typed in place of a declared name. The PAX8_LEARN_SESSION override is stored as "o:" plus the same 64-bit SHA-256 hash the harness session ids get under "h:"; argv_shape records only flag names the invoked command declares under exactly the typed name, every other name as the "<undeclared>" placeholder, and nothing after "--"; failed_flag is never kept as typed; teach.log's missing --query lines record argument counts. Each journal entry is appended whole through credkit.AppendFile, so operator-named text that repeats a credential the program holds is withheld by the kit at the sink (credkit-wiring), no longer by a connector guard.
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.2 (learn/journal.go.tmpl) returns the override raw from JournalSessionKey, so a credential set there is written to journal-*.jsonl on every command, and records every typed flag name, so a credential typed as a flag name (or after --) becomes an argv_shape key and the failed_flag; teach.log records the raw arguments of a teach with no --query. These are names the kit never holds, so they stay hand-fixes (bdd08c08e). Known limits: a guessable override or typed name can be confirmed by hashing guesses; entries an older build wrote stay until the 14-day retention deletes their segment.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: learn/journal.go.tmpl should hash the LEARN_SESSION override as it hashes harness ids, and JournalArgvShape should take the invoked command's declared-flag lookup and record any other name as a placeholder, stopping at "--"; the failed flag should be an opaque identity; teach.log should not echo raw arguments.

handfixes.summary: --all on a Pax8 list starts at page 0, follows the page block to the last page and reports the true total. A walk that cannot be proven complete is an error, not a short list. The generic 100-page cap does not stop a block walk.
handfixes.why: Adversarial review 2026-11-05, s5_all: an absent page counted as 1, so the second request asked for page=2 and rows 10 to 19 of every list were lost: 15 rows of 25, exit 0. internal/pax8blackbox TestPagingAll* failed before the fix (seen/r1-paging-seen-failing.log) and again with the fix reverted (seen/r1-paging-revert.log).

handfixes.summary: export asks for page 0 first with size=200, follows the page block to the last page, and fails rather than writing a partial backup when the walk cannot be proven complete. A resource with fewer rows than one page exports every row.
handfixes.why: Adversarial review 2026-11-05, s12_export: export sent page+1, so it started at page=1: 15 rows of 25, and a resource of 3 rows exported 0, exit 0. internal/pax8blackbox TestPagingExport* failed before the fix (seen/r1-paging-seen-failing.log) and again with the fix reverted (seen/r1-paging-revert.log).

handfixes.summary: Every Pax8 MCP list tool takes page and size in its schema and returns next_cursor while rows remain, read from the page block. The cursor alone continues the same walk with the size and filters it was minted under; repeating them is allowed, changing them or passing page with it is refused. A page the API answers with the wrong number is a tool error. usage-summaries_usage-lines_find pages like the others.
handfixes.why: Adversarial review 2026-11-05, s8_mcp and s9_mcp_cursor: the cursor only walked the slices of the current API page and page was refused as an unknown argument, so subscriptions_find {size:200} reached 200 of 437 rows and no route led further, while the context tool told agents to pass page. internal/pax8blackbox TestPagingMCP* failed before the fix (seen/r1-paging-seen-failing.log) and again with the fix reverted (seen/r1-paging-revert.log).

asserts.contains: pass page or cursor, not both

handfixes.summary: spend and mrr share one reading of the money Pax8 documents (internal/cli/pax8_novel_rules.go). spend sums Invoice.total for status Unpaid, Paid and Carried; Void, Nothing Due and Credited are left out and counted; any other status, or none, is left out and reported with its amount. Money is never added across currencyCode: spend has one row per company and currency, and mrr with more than one currency prints null for totals.mrr and totals.margin and one total per currency in totals.byCurrency. spend shows every company unless --limit asks for fewer. mrr reports a margin only over subscriptions that carry partnerCost and counts the rest in subscriptionsWithoutCost; with no cost on any row the margin is null. Invoice.carriedBalance is not subtracted, because the spec examples do not settle whether Invoice.total includes it. overage averages a product within one currency. Under --agent and --compact, mrr, spend, overage, reconcile and since keep every field their rows define (pax8PrintNovelJSON), so a counter on only some rows survives.
handfixes.why: Adversarial review 2026-11-05, reproduced on the binary: spend counted a Void invoice as spend, cut to 25 companies with no notice, and added currencies under the first currency it saw; mrr printed a margin equal to the MRR when partnerCost was absent, which is every documented example. Tests in internal/cli/pax8_money_test.go failed before the fix (seen/r1-class3-seen-failing.log).

handfixes.summary: At startup every run profile store a run could mean is read through cliutil.HoldProfileFile: HoldBody holds the declared names at any depth, a value under base-url or token-url goes through credkit.HoldURL, and a value under any other credential's name is held, every member of a duplicate key. A profile's name, its free text and its ordinary values still print.
handfixes.why: Codex round 1, confirmed on the binary: a profiles.json with values base-url https://u:<password>@api.pax8.com/v1 printed the password on profile show. HoldBody does not read base-url, and the TOML parse in HoldConfigFile refuses JSON before HoldURL ran. internal/pax8blackbox TestSavedProfileCredentialsNeverPrint failed before the fix (seen/r1-class4-seen-failing.log).

handfixes.summary: Every write of a row in the resources table moves that row past every other row (the upsert's DO UPDATE sets rowid to MAX(rowid) + 1). updated_at keeps its format and its whole-second precision, so a record stored under two names reads as the row written last, within one second too, and rows an earlier release wrote still read by updated_at.
handfixes.why: Codex round 1, reproduced against the store: a live read stored usage summary Y under usage-summaries with currentCharges 10, then a sync updated its older subscriptions_usage_summaries row to 90 in the same second. The update kept the older row's smaller rowid, so the stale 10 won and overage missed a 1.8x overage. internal/cli TestSameSecondUsageSummaryWrittenLastWins and internal/store TestUpsertAdvancesTheRowOnEveryWrite failed before the fix (seen/r1-class5-seen-failing.log).

asserts.contains: ON CONFLICT(resource_type, id) DO UPDATE SET rowid = (SELECT MAX(rowid) + 1 FROM resources), data = excluded.data

handfixes.summary: A dependent whose parent failed, was not readable this run, or was never read counts as failed, not synced, so a sync where everything failed exits non-zero and MCP reports isError. A dependent whose parent was read and really has no rows is still a success. A parent that failed with rows already in the store still gets its children refreshed, and the dependent reports incomplete with nothing pruned. Failed runs keep their counts on stdout for machine callers.
handfixes.why: Adversarial review 2026-11-05, s13_sync_rc: when the token endpoint answered 401, sync exited 0 with errored:6, success:3, total_records:0 and MCP reported no isError, because a dependent with no parent rows counted as a success whatever had happened to its parent. internal/pax8blackbox TestSyncExit* failed before the fix (seen/r1-sync-exit-seen-failing.log) and again with the fix reverted (seen/r1-sync-exit-revert.log).

return syncResult{Resource: dep.Name, Err: parentFailure, Duration: time.Since(started)}

handfixes.summary: sync asks for size=200 on subscriptions, invoices, products, orders and usage summaries, and on every list it reads on until the page block says the last page was read. A row count never decides the end. A walk that cannot be proven complete (no page block, the wrong page answered, an empty page before the last, rows that do not add up to totalElements, a later page that fails or is not JSON) fails its resource with a non-zero exit, keeps the rows it read, prunes nothing under --full, and clears the resume cursor so the next run starts at page 0.
handfixes.why: Adversarial review 2026-11-05, s1_paging: those five lists sent size=10 and believed a page held 100 rows, so a full page of 10 read as the last page. 437 subscriptions stored as 10 with exit 0, mrr reported 200 instead of 8740, and a plain sync --full pruned a complete store to 10 rows. internal/pax8blackbox TestPagingSync* failed before the fix (seen/r1-paging-seen-failing.log) and again with the fix reverted (seen/r1-paging-revert.log).

asserts.contains: %s sync incomplete (%s); %d rows stored", resource, reason, cachedCount), IntegrityFailure: true

handfixes.summary: sync wraps the event writer its parallel workers share in syncSerialWriter (internal/cli/sync_event_writer.go), so two workers never call Write on it at once.
handfixes.why: The generated sync hands cmd.OutOrStdout() (or ErrOrStderr() in machine output) to every --concurrency worker, and each writes sync_start, progress and error events. os.Stdout tolerates that; the writers --deliver (a mirror into a bytes.Buffer) and --receipt-file / --audit-dir (a running SHA-256) install do not, nor does an in-process caller's buffer: Windows CI on PR #655 panicked in bytes.Buffer.grow from syncResource, and go test -race found 28 races on veeam. TestSyncWorkerPoolSerializesEventWrites pins it. A reprint regenerates sync.go and drops the wrap; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-event-writer-serialized).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#5369): the sync template should serialize the event writer its top-level worker pool shares, as its dependent path already does with lockedWriter.

handfixes.summary: the adaptive limiter's blind ramp raises only a rate the last Wait slept on, so sync's rate_rps reports a real pace
handfixes.why: On a header-less API the ramp multiplied the rate by 1.25 every 10 successes with no ceiling: mcp2's hubspot sync printed rate_rps 6.6e24 (about 2,500 requests), and after such a ramp a 429's halving could no longer slow a single request. A rate the requests never reach is no longer raised. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe limiter-paced).

handfixes.summary: a resource the vendor refuses this token (HTTP 403) is recorded as skipped and no longer holds store_status at partial; a resource that errored stays partial and is named.
handfixes.why: A 403 resource never completes, so its sync_state row stayed at 0 and store_status read partial for good after a clean exit 0 (#692). store_status now says complete_with_skips only when every other resource finished, and search, sql and sync_summary name what was skipped or failed. A reprint regenerates sync.go and mcp/tools.go and drops this; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-forbidden-not-partial).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: sync should record a resource the vendor refuses separately from one that failed (not filed yet).

handfixes.summary: sync_progress reports measured rows per second (rows_per_sec, and rate_rps as the same value); the limiter's ceiling is limiter_ceiling_rps.
handfixes.why: The generated sync printed the adaptive limiter's ceiling as rate_rps and as req/s on the human line, so 4.9 was reported while the sync stored 33 rows a second (#694). A reprint regenerates sync.go and brings it back; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-progress-measured-rate).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the sync template should report a measured rate and name the limiter's ceiling separately (not filed yet).

handfixes.summary: sync writes at most one sync_progress line per resource every 5 seconds (the first page always reports; sync_complete carries the final count), instead of one per page.
handfixes.why: Every write to stdout or stderr costs a full credential check whatever its size, and sync wrote one progress line per page: 74% of hubspot sync's CPU at a real server's pace (#696). A reprint regenerates sync.go with one line per page; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies the guard (fleet_handfixes.json sync-progress-throttled).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the sync template's per-page progress line should be throttled, as its dependent walk already is (not filed yet).

retired.reason: tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Press 4.34.0 keeps the environment markers through SaveTokens and generates MarkCredentialsExplicit, so a client ID or secret read from the environment is never written by a token save.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Press 4.34.0 builds a per-command blocked set (blockedDestinationFlags, blockedInputFlags, root control-plane flags), removes those flags from each tool's schema, refuses any undeclared argument name (so "db=/path" is refused) and skips '=' names in cliArgsFromMCP.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Upstreamed as cli-printing-press #4647: every value-carrying branch of cliArgsFromMCP joins the value to its flag (--k=v, one element per list item), and the press generates TestCliArgsFromMCP_ValueCannotSmuggleBlockedFlag.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: The note paused HTTP mode until a reprint because the build served HTTP with no token. Press 4.34.0 HTTP mode refuses to start without <PREFIX>_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN, answers 401 without the right bearer, binds 127.0.0.1 by default and refuses a non-loopback address without TLS; onboard.py now writes HTTP guidance that follows the binary (cc-skills #14) and never writes this note, so the entry would fail on every re-onboard.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Press 4.34.0's cobratree mirror derives one blocked set per command (destination, input, mcp:write-flags, mcp:read-flags and root control-plane flags), leaves those flags out of the tool schema and refuses them, and any undeclared argument, by name.
